introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown: A smooth sphere $S$ of mass $2\ \mathrm{kg}$ is moving with speed $u$ along a smooth horizontal floor when it collides obliquely with a smooth fixed vertical wall. Just before impact the direction of motion of $S$ makes an angle $\theta$ with the plane of the wall. After impact $S$ moves with speed $v$ in a direction making an angle of $60^\circ$ with the plane of the wall. The coefficient of restitution between the sphere and the wall is $\dfrac{1}{3}$.
incertitudes: Question 4 : la dernière demande (« Find the magnitude of the impulse received by the sphere during the impact », 2 marks) n'a pas d'étiquette dans le sujet imprimé ; elle est numérotée iii. Les deux « Show that » sont (i) et (ii).

questions.corrige_markdown:
Resolve the velocity parallel and perpendicular to the wall.

- Before impact (angle $\theta$ with the plane of the wall): parallel component $u\cos\theta$, perpendicular component $u\sin\theta$ (towards the wall).
- After impact (angle $60^\circ$ with the plane of the wall): parallel component $v\cos 60^\circ$, perpendicular component $v\sin 60^\circ$ (away from the wall).

**Smooth wall:** there is no impulse parallel to the wall, so the parallel component is unchanged:

$$
v\cos 60^\circ = u\cos\theta. \tag{1}
$$

**Newton's law of restitution** (perpendicular to the wall, $e=\tfrac13$): speed of separation $= e\times$ speed of approach:

$$
v\sin 60^\circ = \tfrac13\, u\sin\theta. \tag{2}
$$

Dividing (2) by (1):

$$\tan 60^\circ = \tfrac13\tan\theta \;\Longrightarrow\; \tan\theta = 3\tan 60^\circ = 3\sqrt{3}.$$

From part (i), $\tan\theta = 3\sqrt{3}$, so in a right-angled triangle the opposite side is $3\sqrt3$, the adjacent side is $1$ and the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{27+1}=\sqrt{28}=2\sqrt7$. Hence

$$\cos\theta = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{7}}, \qquad \sin\theta = \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{7}}.$$

From equation (1) of part (i), with $\cos 60^\circ=\tfrac12$:

$$\tfrac12 v = u\cos\theta = \frac{u}{2\sqrt7} \;\Longrightarrow\; v = \frac{u}{\sqrt7} = \frac{u\sqrt7}{7}.$$

*Check with (2):* $v\sin60^\circ = \dfrac{u}{\sqrt7}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt3\,u}{2\sqrt7}$ and $\tfrac13u\sin\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt3\,u}{2\sqrt7}$, as required.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the magnitude of the impulse received by the sphere during the impact. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The impulse acts only perpendicular to the wall (the wall is smooth), and equals the change in momentum in that direction. The perpendicular velocity changes from $u\sin\theta = \dfrac{3\sqrt3\,u}{2\sqrt7}$ towards the wall to $v\sin60^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt3\,u}{2\sqrt7}$ away from it, so the total change in velocity is

$$\frac{3\sqrt3\,u}{2\sqrt7} + \frac{\sqrt3\,u}{2\sqrt7} = \frac{4\sqrt3\,u}{2\sqrt7} = \frac{2\sqrt3\,u}{\sqrt7}.$$

With mass $2\ \mathrm{kg}$:

$$I = 2\times\frac{2\sqrt3\,u}{\sqrt7} = \frac{4\sqrt3\,u}{\sqrt7} = \frac{4\sqrt{21}}{7}\,u \approx 2.62\,u\ \ \mathrm{N\,s}.$$

(Equivalently $I = m(1+e)u\sin\theta = 2\times\tfrac43\times u\sin\theta$.)
